recognize_zh: 小而淡染的紅血球中有明顯標靶細胞，中央可見一顆典型兩端尖的鐮刀細胞，另有少數體積較大、略帶藍灰的多染性紅血球，符合鐮刀型 β 地中海型貧血。
features: Microcytic, hypochromic red cells with anisocytosis
Occasional sickle cells with tapered ends (center and top of field)
Scattered larger, slightly grey-blue polychromatophilic cells
Normal segmented neutrophil and scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows microcytic, hypochromic red cells with anisocytosis, frequent target cells, and occasional sickle cells with tapered ends. A few larger polychromatophilic cells are present, consistent with reticulocyte response. The neutrophil and platelets appear morphologically normal. Recent transfusion may dilute the abnormal red cell population. Findings are suggestive of sickle β-thalassemia, confirmed here by mutation analysis.

ddx.vs: HbSS usually has normocytic indices with more numerous sickle cells and Howell-Jolly bodies from autosplenectomy, whereas microcytosis with hypochromia favors Sβ-thalassemia; HPLC (HbA2 elevated, HbA absent/reduced) and molecular testing separate them.
HbSC shows many target cells and characteristic HbC crystals and folded/boat-shaped cells, with fewer classic sickle cells and HbC on HPLC.
β-thalassemia shows microcytosis, target cells, and nucleated red cells but no sickle cells, and HbS is absent on HPLC.
Iron deficiency has microcytic hypochromic cells and pencil cells but lacks sickle cells and prominent target cells, with low ferritin.
